groups.catalog-capability-field-flags: All four mutants toggle a dataclass field() flag on CatalogEntry's capability metadata: capability_version (L66) and capability_changes (L67), both declared field(default=None, compare=False, hash=False). These flags affect ONLY the generated CatalogEntry.__eq__ (compare) and __hash__ (hash); they do not change the stored value or attribute access. Across aisef2/, validation/ and tests/ at this snapshot NOTHING hashes a CatalogEntry, uses one as a dict key or set member, or compares two CatalogEntry objects with == / assertEqual. catalog.problems_of() dedups on explicit (probe_id, probe_digest) tuples; active()/catalogue()/probes_by_id()/registry() build dicts keyed by subject_kind or probe_id; entry_for() uses next(...e.module==...). Every other consumer (bundle_cli.migrate, diagnostics, run, review_verify, bundle, static_admission, and all validation/qualification/* and validation/v2/* readers) iterates entries and reads attribute VALUES or constructs new entries via dataclasses.replace -- none routes through __eq__/__hash__. bundle_cli.migrate reads entry.capability_version (bundle_cli.py:235) and entry.capability_changes (bundle_cli.py:200) as VALUES into the operator-visible migrate report, so the report is byte-for-byte unaffected by compare/hash. The registered kill file tests.v2.test_v21_migrate_semantics PASSED on every one of the four mutants (Ran 51 tests OK, identical to the unmutated baseline): it exercises capability VALUES and migrate behaviour, and its FailClosed assertions compare sets of contract-id strings, never entries -- so by construction it cannot observe a compare/hash flag change. Exception named and checked: validation/qualification/v21_conformance_ruling.py:137 describes this change and states '(neither is compared: compare=False)', but that is descriptive prose; its two cited behaviour_tests (Declarations.test_every_probe_of_the_catalog_declares_every_capability_version_above_1 and .test_the_catalog_entry_is_what_the_module_declares) check the capability VALUES against the module's CAPABILITY_VERSION/CAPABILITY_CHANGES, not the compare/hash flags, and nothing machine-verifies the flag value. Therefore no consumer, contract, document or operator depends on the eq/hash participation of these two fields: AUDITED, not REFUTED, and not EQUIVALENT (each mutant is distinguishable by a constructed observation, e.g. dataclasses.replace(e, capability_version=99)==e, or hash() of the file_artifact entry).

notes: 4/4 new survivors AUDITED; 0 EQUIVALENT, 0 REFUTED. The four flags affect only CatalogEntry.__eq__/__hash__, and no consumer/contract/document/operator at snapshot 4ec961e hashes or ==-compares a CatalogEntry (verified by repo-wide grep over aisef2/ validation/ tests/ and by reading every catalog consumer). The registered kill file tests.v2.test_v21_migrate_semantics PASSED unchanged on all four (51 tests OK, == unmutated baseline), confirming survival. Acceptance-scope note for the owner (not a REFUTED gap, per the positional rule -- there is no current reader): (1) index 1 of capability_changes (hash=False->True) is the only mutant with a correctness edge -- it would make the frozen file_artifact entry unhashable; hash=False is a deliberate defensive flag for a dict field, documented nowhere as a test. (2) The conformance ruling v21_conformance_ruling.py:137 asserts '(neither is compared: compare=False)' but its cited behaviour tests verify capability VALUES, not the flags, so the compare=False claim is itself unpinned. If the owner wants these pinned, the smallest owed tests would be: (a) construct two entries via dataclasses.replace differing only in capability_version/capability_changes and assert == and equal hash (pins compare=False, hash=False for the eq/hash exclusion); (b) assert hash(active()[FILE_ARTIFACT_kind]) does not raise (pins hashability despite the dict). Recommend recording as a known limit rather than adding tests to reach a number.
